mainTopic: When a ברכה covers other foods: dessert-bread and קביעות סעודה, when a meal ends, and the new משנה on one ברכה exempting another
overview: This amud opens by finishing an answer from the previous page: יין gets its own ברכה even during a meal, because it is important enough to bring a ברכה for itself. The גמרא then tells two stories about פת הבאה בכסנין, sweet dessert-bread. Together they teach that this bread counts as real bread, needing המוציא and ברכת המזון, only when a person makes a meal of it (קביעות סעודה). Next, a series of stories asks when a meal is over, so that eating more would need a new ברכה. The options are finishing (גמר), removing the table (סלק), relying on the host's table, and the habit of applying oil after eating. The גמרא rejects all of these and rules like רב: ברכת המזון must come right after the after-meal hand washing. אביי adds an aggadic teaching that blessing comes right away to a home that hosts תלמידי חכמים. Finally a new משנה teaches which ברכות cover other foods, such as wine before the meal covering wine after it and bread covering appetizers, and when one person can say the ברכה for a whole group.

steps.title: Wine is special because it brings its own blessing
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of the previous answer. יין is different from other foods at a meal because it is important enough to get a ברכה of its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Wine is different,] because it causes a blessing for itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the previous page: wine gets its own ברכה even in the middle of a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the המוציא on bread covers the rest of a meal. יין is an exception because it is so important that we make ברכות over it by itself, such as at קידוש and הבדלה. So the bread's ברכה does not cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: a blessing for itself (its own blessing)

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. It is the end of an answer that began on the previous page. It is not a new teaching.

phrases.english: for it causes a blessing for itself.
phrases.notes: Refers to wine, which gets its own ברכה at קידוש and הבדלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּגוֹרֵם בְּרָכָה לְעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the previous daf about why wine at a meal needs its own ברכה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing feature (חילוק): wine has independent importance
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine during a meal is not covered by המוציא, because it is important enough to get its own ברכה.

steps.title: רב הונא eats thirteen sweet loaves without ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא ate thirteen large sweet loaves of פת הבאה בכסנין and did not say ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא ate thirteen loaves, each one made from a third of a קב of flour, and did not say ברכת המזון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up the next move. רב הונא ate a lot of dessert-bread and treated it as a snack, so he skipped ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each loaf used a third of a קב, so these were big loaves. רב הונא held that dessert-bread is never real bread and never needs ברכת המזון. The next step challenges that view.

keyTerms.meaning: a קב, a measure of flour

phrases.english: Rav Huna ate thirteen loaves
of the size of three per kav
phrases.notes: Each loaf used a third of a קב, so they were large.

phrases.english: and he did not recite the blessing.
phrases.notes: He did not say ברכת המזון.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אֲכַל תְּלֵיסַר רִיפְתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from wine to a story about פת הבאה בכסנין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא held that a large amount of dessert-bread still does not need ברכת המזון.

steps.title: רב נחמן: that is real hunger
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rejects what רב הונא did. Eating that much is eating to fill up, not eating dessert.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: That is hunger!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back. He says that eating so much is not a snack; it is satisfying real hunger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody eats thirteen big loaves as a treat after a meal. Once you eat to fill yourself up, the food is acting like a meal, so the 'just dessert' reasoning falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: that is hunger (you ate to satisfy real hunger)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
That is hunger!
phrases.notes: Such an amount is eaten to satisfy hunger, not as dessert.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: עָדֵי כַּפְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's behavior in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that dessert-bread never needs ברכת המזון no matter how much is eaten.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב הונא ignored the quantity. That much food satisfies hunger and functions as a meal.

steps.title: The rule: if people make a meal of it, bless
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives the general rule. Any amount that others would make a meal of requires ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, whatever others make a meal of requires a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן turns his objection into a clear rule: the test is whether people would treat this amount as a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule does not depend on the type of bread alone. It depends on how much is eaten and how it is used. The test is an objective one ('others'), so it does not matter whether this particular person felt he was having a meal.

keyTerms.meaning: make it into a fixed meal
one must say the blessing (ברכת המזון)

steps.whatToRemember: פת הבאה בכסנין becomes like regular bread, needing ברכת המזון, when a person eats the amount that people normally make a meal of.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the halachic rule of קביעות סעודה with מזונות-type baked goods, such as cake or crackers. Eating a meal-sized amount requires המוציא and ברכת המזון.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כֹּל שֶׁאֲחֵרִים קוֹבְעִים עָלָיו סְעוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rather, anything that others establish a meal upon,
one must recite the blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כֹּל שֶׁאֲחֵרִים קוֹבְעִים עָלָיו סְעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רב נחמן's objection into a general rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whatever amount people normally make a meal of requires ברכת המזון, even if it is dessert-bread.

steps.title: At a wedding preparation, people say המוציא on dessert-bread
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה was at the house of רב יהודה בר חביבא arranging his son's wedding. פת הבאה בכסנין was served, and he heard people saying המוציא over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה was busy arranging his son's wedding at the house of רב יהודה בר חביבא. They brought dessert-bread before them. When it came, he heard them saying המוציא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second story and sets the scene for רב יהודה's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the dessert-bread is eaten as dessert, not as a meal. Even so, the people said המוציא, which is the ברכה for real bread. This is what will surprise רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: busy with his son (arranging his marriage)

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה הֲוָה עָסֵיק לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda was occupied with his son
at the house of Rav Yehuda bar Chaviva.
They brought before them bread that comes as dessert.
When it arrived,
he heard them reciting "Hamotzi."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה הֲוָה עָסֵיק לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about dessert-bread. This time the case involves no meal-sized amount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people present said המוציא on dessert-bread eaten as dessert.

steps.title: רב יהודה asks what blessing he heard
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks whether the 'צִיצִי' sound he heard was really המוציא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: What is this 'צִיצִי' sound I hear? Are you perhaps saying 'המוציא לחם מן הארץ'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה asks a question that sounds surprised. He wants to confirm whether they really said המוציא on dessert-bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'צִיצִי' is the sound of the word 'מוציא' heard in a whisper. His question hints that he disagrees: he thinks this bread does not get המוציא.

phrases.english: He said to them: What is this "tzitzi" that I hear?

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא ״הַמּוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ״ קָא מְבָרְכִיתוּ?
phrases.english: Perhaps you are reciting "Who brings forth bread from the earth"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ: מַאי ״צִיצִי״ דְּקָא שָׁמַעְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the המוציא heard in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether they were really saying המוציא over dessert-bread.

steps.title: They answer yes, citing רבי מונא and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: They confirm that they said המוציא. They support it with a ברייתא from רבי מונא and with שמואל's ruling that the halacha follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Yes. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי מונא said in the name of רבי יהודה that over dessert-bread one says המוציא. And שמואל said: the הלכה follows רבי מונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The people answer 'yes' and bring sources to show they acted correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their support has two layers. A ברייתא gives רבי מונא's opinion, and שמואל rules like him. If both are accurate, dessert-bread always gets המוציא.

phrases.english: They said to him: Yes.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי מוּנָא אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Mona said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda:
over bread that comes as dessert one recites "Hamotzi,"
and Shmuel said: The halacha follows Rabbi Mona.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: אִין. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's question and defends what they did.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, they said המוציא, relying on רבי מונא and on שמואל's ruling in his favor.

steps.title: רב יהודה corrects the quote: the הלכה is NOT like רבי מונא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says they quoted שמואל wrong. שמואל actually said the הלכה does not follow רבי מונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'The הלכה is not like רבי מונא' is what was stated.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה rejects their proof by correcting what שמואל actually said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue with the ברייתא itself. He fixes the version of שמואל's ruling. Since שמואל ruled against רבי מונא, dessert-bread does not get המוציא.

keyTerms.meaning: it was stated (the correct version of the teaching)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְהוּ: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מוּנָא אִתְּמַר.
phrases.english: He said to them: "The halacha is not like Rabbi Mona" is what was stated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מוּנָא אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only שמואל's ruling, not the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They quoted שמואל wrong. The correct version is 'אין הלכה כרבי מונא.'

steps.title: Challenge from רב יהודה's own ruling on wafers
steps.stepSummary: They challenge רב יהודה from something he himself quoted from שמואל: לחמניות can be used for an עירוב and get המוציא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But isn't it you, Master, who said in שמואל's name that wafers may be used for an עירוב and one says המוציא over them?
steps.whatsHappening: The people attack רב יהודה's position using his own earlier teaching from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לחמניות are also a sweet, dessert-like bread, yet רב יהודה quoted שמואל that they get המוציא. That seems to contradict his claim that שמואל ruled against רבי מונא.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it the Master who said
one may make an עירוב (with them)

phrases.english: They said to him: But isn't the Master the one
who said in the name of Shmuel
wafers: one may make an eiruv with them,
and one recites "Hamotzi" over them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מָר הוּא דְּאָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's correction in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that שמואל held dessert-bread does not get המוציא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction: רב יהודה himself quoted שמואל saying that לחמניות, a similar bread, do get המוציא.

steps.title: Different there: a meal was made of them
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the wafers ruling refers to a case where someone made a meal of them. Without a meal, there is no המוציא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because he made his meal of them. But where he did not make his meal of them, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה resolves the contradiction by showing that the two rulings speak about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wafers ruling applies when the person makes a meal of them. At the wedding gathering the bread was eaten as dessert, so it gets no המוציא. This matches רב נחמן's rule from earlier: making a meal of it is what turns dessert-bread into real bread.

keyTerms.meaning: he made his fixed meal (of them)

steps.whatToRemember: פת הבאה בכסנין gets המוציא only when a person makes a meal of it (קביעות סעודה). Eaten as a snack, it does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the הלכה that cake and crackers are מזונות as a snack, but become המוציא and ברכת המזון when eaten as a meal.

phrases.english: It is different there, since he established his meal upon them,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלָא קָבַע סְעוֹדְתֵּיהּ עֲלַיְיהוּ — לָא.
phrases.english: but where he did not establish his meal upon them, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּקָבַע סְעוֹדְתֵּיהּ עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (שאני): a meal versus a snack
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's wafers ruling seemed to say that sweet bread always gets המוציא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sweet bread gets המוציא only when a meal is made of it. Otherwise it does not, consistent with 'אין הלכה כרבי מונא.'

steps.title: רב פפא eats after the meal is finished
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב פפא visits רב הונא בריה דרב נתן. After the meal is done, food is brought out, and רב פפא eats it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא came to the house of רב הונא son of רב נתן. After they finished their meal, they brought out something to eat. רב פפא took it and ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to set up the next move. רב פפא eats after the meal seems to be over, and the hosts are about to question him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meal is finished, but the table has not been taken away yet. Eating at this point looks like a problem, because the meal may already count as over. The story is a setup for the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa happened to come

phrases.aramaic: לְבֵי רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן.
phrases.english: to the house of Rav Huna son of Rav Natan.
After they finished their meal
they brought before them something to eat
Rav Pappa took it and ate.
phrases.notes: He ate without making a new ברכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: eating after the meal has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: רב פפא ate after the meal was finished but before the table was removed.

steps.title: The hosts question רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The hosts challenge him: once you have finished eating, aren't you forbidden to eat more without a new ברכה?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Don't you hold that once a person has finished his meal, he is forbidden to eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The hosts challenge רב פפא's behavior using a known rule: after finishing, you may not keep eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their version of the rule says the cutoff is גמר, the moment you decide you are done. By that version, רב פפא's eating looks wrong. The question is worded as a question, but it works as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden to eat (without a new ברכה)

phrases.english: They said to him:
Does the master not hold
that once one finished, he is forbidden to eat?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר גָּמַר אָסוּר מִלֶּאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's action from the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's eating after the meal was finished
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If finishing (גמר) ends the meal, then eating afterward without a new ברכה should be forbidden.

steps.title: The rule says removed, not finished
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the correct wording of the rule is סלק (the table was removed), not גמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The rule was stated with the word 'removed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends himself by fixing the wording of the rule. The meal ends only when the table is taken away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended on the word גמר. רב פפא says the real word is סלק. Since the table was still there, he had not finished, and he could keep eating under the first ברכה.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא does not deny that the meal can end. He only says the trigger is removing the table, not mentally deciding you are done.

phrases.english: He said to them: 'Removed' was stated.

steps.triggerLanguage: סִלֵּק אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by correcting the wording of the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The meal ends at גמר, when one finishes eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: The meal ends at סלק, when the table is removed. Before that, one may keep eating.

steps.title: רבא eats after the table was removed
steps.stepSummary: A second story: at the ריש גלותא's house, after the table is removed, food is sent over. רבא eats and רבי זירא does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא and רבי זירא came to the house of the ריש גלותא. After the table was removed from before them, a portion of food was sent to them from the ריש גלותא's house. רבא ate, and רבי זירא did not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story to set up the next challenge. This time even the table has been removed, yet רבא still eats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case goes a step past רב פפא's case. Here סלק has already happened, so by רב פפא's rule eating should be forbidden. רבי זירא holds back, and רבא does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Bavel

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא וְרַבִּי זֵירָא אִיקְּלַעוּ לְבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא.
phrases.english: Rava and Rabbi Zeira happened to come to the house of the Exilarch.
After they removed the table from before them

phrases.aramaic: שַׁדַּרוּ לְהוּ רִיסְתָּנָא מִבֵּי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא.
phrases.english: they sent them a portion from the Exilarch's house.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָכֵיל וְרַבִּי זֵירָא לָא אָכֵיל.
phrases.english: Rava ate and Rabbi Zeira did not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא וְרַבִּי זֵירָא אִיקְּלַעוּ לְבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story that tests the rule of סלק from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: רבא ate after the table was removed.

steps.title: רבי זירא questions רבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רבא: once the table is removed, isn't eating forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Don't you hold that once the table is removed, one is forbidden to eat?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא uses the rule of סלק, the same wording רב פפא gave in step 13, to challenge רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even under the more lenient wording, the table was already removed here. So רבא's eating seems to break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Once the table is removed, one may not eat (without a new ברכה)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Does the master not hold
that once removed, one is forbidden to eat?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר סִלֵּק אָסוּר מִלֶּאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's action in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's eating after the table was removed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of סלק says the meal ends when the table is removed, and here it was removed.

steps.title: Guests depend on the host's table
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that guests rely on the ריש גלותא's table. As long as the host's meal continues, theirs does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We rely on the table of the ריש גלותא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains that his own table being removed does not matter. What counts is the host's table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of סלק still stands. רבא only clarifies whose table counts. For guests, it is the host's table, and the host was still eating, since he was sending out food.

phrases.english: He said to him:
We rely on the table of the Exilarch.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנַן אַתַּכָּא דְּרֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא סָמְכִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: whose table counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each guest's meal ends when his own table is removed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A guest's meal follows the host's table, so it is not over while the host is still eating.

steps.title: Someone used to oil is not finished until he uses it
steps.stepSummary: רב says a person who usually puts oil on his hands after eating has not finished his meal until he does. רב כהנא said the same about his household.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Someone who is used to oil, the oil holds him back (his meal is not over until he applies it). רב אשי said: When we were at רב כהנא's house, he told us: People like us, who are used to oil, the oil holds us back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another view of when a meal ends. For people with a custom of applying oil, the meal continues until the oil is applied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a third possible end point, besides גמר and סלק. It depends on a person's personal habit. רב כהנא's statement shows the rule was actually practiced.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds him back (his meal is not yet over)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: הָרָגִיל בְּשֶׁמֶן — שֶׁמֶן מְעַכְּבוֹ.
phrases.english: Rav said: One accustomed to oil, the oil holds him back.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כִּי הָוֵינַן בֵּי רַב כָּהֲנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: When we were at Rav Kahana's house,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לַן: כְּגוֹן אֲנַן דִּרְגִילִינַן בְּמִשְׁחָא —
phrases.english: he said to us: For example, we who are accustomed to oil,
the oil holds us back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הָרָגִיל בְּשֶׁמֶן שֶׁמֶן מְעַכְּבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another view on what ends a meal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For someone used to applying oil, the meal is not over until the oil is applied.

steps.title: The הלכה: the ברכה comes right after washing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects all the earlier views. The הלכה follows רב: there are three things that must come right after something else. ברכת המזון comes right after the after-meal hand washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה does not follow any of these teachings. Rather, it follows what רבי חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: There are three things that must come immediately. Right after סמיכה comes שחיטה. Right after גאולה comes תפלה. Right after hand washing comes the ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling. The meal ends with the after-meal hand washing, and then the ברכה must be said right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גמר, סלק, the host's table, and the oil are all rejected as the cutoff. Once someone washes מים אחרונים, he must say ברכת המזון immediately, with no eating in between. Before washing, the meal is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is not like this
The ברכה of redemption after שמע (גאל ישראל)
Hand washing (here: מים אחרונים after the meal)

steps.whatToRemember: The final rule: a meal ends with the after-meal hand washing, and ברכת המזון must follow right away. The earlier opinions (גמר, סלק, the host's table, oil) are not the הלכה.
steps.confusionAlert: The נטילת ידים here is the washing after the meal (מים אחרונים), not the washing before eating bread.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling settles the practical question of when you can no longer eat without a new ברכה, and it is the source for not talking or pausing between מים אחרונים and ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: And the halacha is not like all these teachings,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: rather, like that which Rabbi Chiya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav:
There are three things that follow immediately:
Immediately after leaning hands comes slaughter,
immediately after redemption comes prayer,
immediately after washing the hands comes the blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית הִלְכְתָא כְּכׇל הָנֵי שְׁמַעְתָּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects all the previous views and gives the final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The meal ends with מים אחרונים, and ברכת המזון must be said immediately after.

steps.title: אביי: blessing comes right after תלמידי חכמים
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a fourth 'right after' as a side teaching: blessing comes right after תלמידי חכמים arrive, as לבן said to יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We too will say: Right after תלמידי חכמים comes blessing, as it says: 'ה׳ has blessed me because of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the three 'right after' pairs, אביי adds a non-legal teaching: a home that hosts תלמידי חכמים is blessed right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This borrows the תכף pattern for an aggadic idea. The proof is לבן telling יעקב that ה׳ blessed him because of יעקב.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We too will say:
Immediately after Torah scholars comes blessing.
As it is said: 'The Lord has blessed me because of you.'
phrases.notes: בראשית ל:כז, לבן speaking to יעקב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אָנוּ נֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an aggadic 'right after' modeled on רב's three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blessing comes immediately with the arrival of תלמידי חכמים.

steps.title: A second proof from יוסף in the Egyptian's house
steps.stepSummary: Another verse supports אביי: ה׳ blessed the Egyptian's house because of יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say the proof is from here, as it says: 'ה׳ blessed the house of the Egyptian because of יוסף.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another verse as proof for אביי's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about יוסף and פוטיפר shows the same idea, a house blessed because of a righteous person. It may be a stronger proof, since the verse says the blessing came right after יוסף was put in charge.

phrases.english: If you wish, say from here, as it is said:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיְבָרֶךְ ה׳ אֶת בֵּית הַמִּצְרִי בִּגְלַל יוֹסֵף״.
phrases.english: 'The Lord blessed the house of the Egyptian on account of Joseph.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative verse proving אביי's point.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's teaching that blessing comes right after תלמידי חכמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית לט:ה, ה׳ blessed פוטיפר's house because of יוסף

steps.title: Wine before the meal covers wine after the meal
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens: a ברכה on wine drunk before the meal also covers wine drunk after the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone said a ברכה on the wine before the meal, he has covered the wine after the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. Its first rule is that one ברכה on wine before the meal is enough for the wine he drinks after the meal too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that one ברכה can 'exempt' (פוטר) a later food or drink of the same kind, so he does not need a new ברכה. This is the first of several 'this ברכה covers that food' rules in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the text the גמרא will discuss)
Exempted / covered, so no new ברכה is needed
That is before / that is after

steps.confusionAlert: 'Exempted' here does not mean he is free from saying any ברכה at all. It means the ברכה he already said also counts for the later wine.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of a new משנה.

phrases.english: If one recited a blessing over the wine before the meal,
he exempted the wine after the meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּרַךְ עַל הַיַּיִן שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמָּזוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברכה on wine before the meal covers wine after the meal.

steps.title: Appetizers before the meal cover appetizers after the meal
steps.stepSummary: The same rule applies to פרפרת: the ברכה on appetizers before the meal covers appetizers after the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said a ברכה on the appetizers before the meal, he has covered the appetizers after the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the same pattern for side foods (פרפרת). One ברכה before the meal covers the same kind of food after the meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is building a list. Wine and פרפרת follow the same rule: what comes before the meal covers what comes after it.

keyTerms.meaning: Appetizers / side snacks, not the main bread

phrases.english: If one recited a blessing over the appetizers before the meal,
he exempted the appetizers after the meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּרַךְ עַל הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמָּזוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'before covers after' rule from wine to appetizers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברכה on appetizers before the meal covers appetizers after the meal.

steps.title: Bread covers appetizers, but appetizers do not cover bread
steps.stepSummary: The ברכה on bread covers the appetizers, but a ברכה on appetizers does not cover the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said a ברכה on the bread, he has covered the appetizers. If he said it on the appetizers, he has not covered the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now compares two different foods. Bread is the main food, so its ברכה covers the side foods. It does not work the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule only goes one way: the main food (פת) covers the side food (פרפרת). A ברכה on the less important food cannot cover the more important one.

keyTerms.meaning: The bread, the main food of the meal

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic idea behind why we usually do not say separate ברכות on foods eaten during a bread meal.

phrases.english: If one recited a blessing over the bread,
he exempted the appetizers.

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת — לֹא פָּטַר אֶת הַפַּת.
phrases.english: If he blessed over the appetizers, he did not exempt the bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּרַךְ עַל הַפַּת — פָּטַר אֶת הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from 'same food, different times' to 'different foods': bread compared with appetizers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread's ברכה covers appetizers. Appetizers' ברכה does not cover bread.

steps.title: בית שמאי: not even a cooked dish
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say that a cooked dish (מעשה קדרה) is not covered either.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: not even a cooked dish.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי add a short comment. In their view, the ברכה does not cover even a cooked dish eaten in the meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following Sefaria's reading, בית שמאי hold that the ברכה on the appetizers does not cover even a cooked dish. The משנה gives only a few words, and the גמרא will later explain exactly what בית שמאי mean and how they differ from the first opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי, who often disagree with בית הלל
A cooked dish (literally, 'something made in a pot')

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
Not even a cooked dish.
phrases.notes: Very short wording. The גמרא will explain what it means.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אַף לֹא מַעֲשֵׂה קְדֵרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית שמאי's added view on which foods the ברכה does not cover.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, the ברכה does not cover even a cooked dish.

steps.title: Sitting: each person blesses himself. Reclining: one blesses for all
steps.stepSummary: People who just sit together each say their own ברכה. People who recline together as a group have one person say it for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were sitting, each one says a ברכה for himself. If they reclined, one person says the ברכה for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new rule about groups. It depends on how the people are eating together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply sitting near each other does not make it one shared meal, so each person blesses on his own. Reclining together (הסבה) turns it into a real group meal, so one person can say the ברכה for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Sitting (eating near each other, not as a set group)
They reclined together, making it one shared meal

steps.whatToRemember: One ברכה can cover other foods: the same food before and after the meal, and bread covers appetizers but not the reverse. For a group, reclining together lets one person say the ברכה for everyone, while just sitting means each person blesses himself.

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ יוֹשְׁבִין — כׇּל אֶחָד מְבָרֵךְ לְעַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: If they were sitting, each one recites a blessing for himself.
If they reclined, one recites a blessing for all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ יוֹשְׁבִין — כׇּל אֶחָד מְבָרֵךְ לְעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from which foods a ברכה covers to which people one person's ברכה can cover.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sitting means each person blesses separately. Reclining together means one person blesses for everyone.
